revision_summary: No critical fabricated quotes were found (all quotes checked verify against the transcript), so this does not need a full rerun, but several targeted fixes are needed: (1) Fix schema misuse — cherry_pick_moments[1] (01:19, brothers-on-title) should reference verify.title_co_owners rather than protocols.spouse_decision, since spouse_decision is keyed to spousal deferral language, not co-ownership disclosure; note the adult_child_decision_maker protocol as an analogous pattern instead. (2) Fix schema misuse in cherry_pick_moments[4] (04:07) — 'enthusiasm_signal' is not a valid schema classification and 'cross_sell_signals' is the wrong reference (that section is for roofing/battery triggers); reclassify against coaching_philosophy.bill_anchoring instead, and soften the confidence that the kWh spike figures map cleanly to bill-dollar pain given the ambiguous month/number transcript at 04:14-04:44. (3) Flag the 05:30 customer line ('It should say this is lying but not real') as likely transcription garble rather than analyzing it as customer sentiment/confusion — this weakens a state_change entry built on unreliable text. (4) Add the missing button_up gaps to coaching_focus or script_coverage detail — the 'is that fair?' handshake and the 'no driving / sit at computer' instruction are both absent, which is a more complete miss than the single script_coverage row conveys, and per schema this is predictive of no-show risk — worth a coaching_focus entry, not just a script_coverage note. (5) Consider crediting 09:04 ('I'm not entirely too sure... that's exactly what we're gonna go over with you in the meeting') as a positive knowledge_gap_handling example per analysis_directives, rather than folding it entirely into an objection_inversion_miss critique. (6) Soften handoff_brief.closer_should_know language that prescribes how the closer should open ('should lead with concrete pricing context early') to avoid locking the closer's approach per handoff_brief_discipline. (7) The 00:04 opening ('Did you miss a call from us?') should be surfaced as a legitimacy-framing gap distinct from the 00:15 script_coverage 'asked' mark for intro_legitimacy — the actual opening line skipped the standard company/form/state framing and likely caused the customer's initial confusion.
